bug_semantics: CVE-2026-44645 / GHSA-8xx9-69p8-7jp3 is a CPU/event-loop denial of service in LiquidJS's renderLimit control. The for and tablerow parsers store their bodies as Template[] arrays. An empty body therefore makes each collection iteration call Render.renderTemplates([], ctx, emitter). In vulnerable releases, the only ctx.renderLimit.check(...) was inside `for (const tpl of templates)`, so an empty array executed no check while the outer for/tag or tablerow/tag loop still traversed the entire attacker-selected collection; tablerow additionally emitted table markup. A low-privileged author of an untrusted Liquid template could use an empty `{% for i in (1..N) %}{% endfor %}` or empty tablerow to consume CPU far beyond the configured time budget, bounded only by other resource controls such as memoryLimit.
flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 (`feat: DoS prevention, #250`). That commit introduced the renderLimit option, its Limiter state, the documented security guarantee, and the sole enforcement call in src/render/render.ts inside the per-template loop. The pre-existing Render.renderTemplates loop naturally did nothing for an empty Template[]; e443068 made that placement security-relevant by promising a per-render time limit but checking only when a body node existed. `git log e443068... -L 14,23:src/render/render.ts` attributes that exact check insertion to e443068, and `git log e443068... -S'ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now())' -- src/render/render.ts` plus `-S'renderLimit?: number' -- src/liquid-options.ts` independently return e443068. It is a one-parent direct commit, not a move, revert, release/backport, or reconstructable squash aggregate.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2` shows author `Yang Jun <harttleharttle@gmail.com>`, committer `Jun Yang <harttleharttle@gmail.com>`, subject/body `feat: DoS prevention, #250`, and no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity. The Cursor co-author trailer on the 2026 fix commit is deliberately excluded by the BIC-only attribution rule.
evidence: Reproduction from the validated clone: (1) `git show e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 -- src/render/render.ts src/context/context.ts src/liquid-options.ts docs/source/tutorials/dos.md test/integration/liquid/dos.spec.ts` shows the new renderLimit API/security documentation and adds `ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now())` only inside `for (const tpl of templates)`. `git show e443068...:src/tags/for.ts` shows `this.templates = []`, body nodes pushed by the parser, and every collection item yielding `r.renderTemplates(this.templates, ctx, emitter)`; the analogous tablerow file does the same. Thus an empty body passes [] and skips the only limiter check. (2) Direct parent verification: `git cat-file -p e443068...` names sole parent fad00aa14e8beac0514ec4196944b33276f1ff2c; `git grep -n renderLimit fad00aa14e8beac0514ec4196944b33276f1ff2c -- src` returns no match. The parent has neither the option nor the vulnerable guard/security promise. (3) Origin cross-check: `git log e443068... -L 14,23:src/render/render.ts` and both pickaxes `-S'ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now())'` and `-S'renderLimit?: number'` identify e443068 as first writer. (4) Fix: `git show 5b9c3469085e01c79e2d0af28e2a13f730e1793d` adds `ctx.renderLimit.check(getPerformance().now())` at renderTemplates entry before the loop and adds empty-for and empty-tablerow regressions. Its sole parent dbbf6288030591bf6da28d8c1cce5a17bca97bb6 lacks that entry check. (5) Version boundary: `git tag --contains e443068... | sort -V` begins at v10.15.0; e443068 is not an ancestor of v10.14.0 but is the parent of release commit 542a75fd44eecdeac8e5ff9ab19ed334c194d86c (package version 10.15.0). The advisory reports vulnerable `<= 10.25.7`; operationally the renderLimit feature and this bypass span v10.15.0 through v10.25.7. `git grep -n renderLimit.check v10.25.7 -- src/render/render.ts` shows only the in-loop check. `git tag --contains 5b9c346... | sort -V` begins at v10.26.0; the fix is absent from v10.25.7 and is an ancestor of v10.26.0 release commit c20c0af02d33e8d2ca6b08925eadca8755257c39, where grep shows both entry and in-loop checks. (6) BIC attribution: `git cat-file -p e443068...` has human author/committer and no AI marker. For completeness, the closing mainline commit 5b9c346 is patch/tree-equivalent to PR-branch commit 7910e4996cdb37e4c020d4f6d3ae47b5d8e54e8f and carries `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>`, but that is fix-only evidence and cannot affect the BIC verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is not the ancient fact that iterating an empty array performs no work; it is the renderLimit security implementation that relied exclusively on body-node execution. e443068 is therefore the causal first-writer and smallest public commit that created the bypass: its parent has no renderLimit at all, while e443068 simultaneously promises the limit and installs the incomplete enforcement point. The direct fix moves an additional check to renderTemplates entry, which is reached once per outer loop iteration even when templates is empty, closing both for and tablerow variants. Release ancestry corroborates introduction in 10.15.0, exposure through 10.25.7, and closure in 10.26.0. Because the e443068 commit object has no canonical AI attribution and no bot identity, the required BIC-only judgment is NOT_AI; Cursor's explicit participation in the later fix is irrelevant.
